The test image shows a soybean leaf held by hand, with a diffuse reddish-purple/bronze discoloration covering the upper leaf surface — a bronzing/leathery appearance rather than discrete spots. Some small dark elongated lesions are also visible. This strongly suggests Cercospora leaf blight.

Let me check one reference image to confirm.

The Cercospora reference shows discrete red-brown spots on green-yellow background, while the test image shows more uniform reddish-purple bronzing. However, the Cercospora symptom description specifically mentions "reddish-purple or bronze discoloration, giving a leathery sunburned appearance" — which matches the test image well. The reference may show an earlier stage.

The test image shows a young soybean plant with diffuse reddish-purple/bronze coloration across the entire upper leaf surface — a "sunburned, leathery" look. This is the hallmark of Cercospora leaf blight. The small elongated darker lesions are also consistent.
